description: An examination of settlement types, patterns and locating factors, the process of urbanisation and rural-urban migration, and the growth, problems and planning of towns and cities in Tanzania and Africa.

mcq.questionText: What is the meaning of the term 'settlement' in geography?

options.text: A place where people live and carry out their daily activities
An area set aside only for growing crops
A region covered by natural forest
The movement of people from one country to another

mcq.explanation: A settlement is any place where people live, ranging from a single homestead to a large city, together with the buildings and activities found there.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a permanent settlement?

options.text: A pastoralists' camp moved with the seasons
A town such as Mwanza
A temporary fishing camp on a sandbank
A miners' tent at a new gold deposit

mcq.explanation: Permanent settlements like Mwanza are occupied throughout the year, while pastoral camps, fishing camps and miners' tents are temporary.

mcq.questionText: A settlement pattern in which houses are grouped closely together is called:

options.text: Dispersed pattern
Linear pattern
Nucleated pattern
Radial pattern

mcq.explanation: In a nucleated (clustered) pattern, houses are built close together, often around a feature such as a market, water point or crossroads.

mcq.questionText: Which settlement pattern develops along a road, river or valley?

options.text: Linear pattern
Nucleated pattern
Dispersed pattern
Scattered pattern

mcq.explanation: A linear settlement stretches in a line because houses are built along a line of communication such as a road, railway, river or the edge of a valley.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following factors most directly explains why early settlements were located near rivers and lakes?

options.text: Availability of water for domestic use, livestock and farming
Presence of high mountains for defence
Existence of large deserts nearby
Cold climate suitable for industry

mcq.explanation: Water is essential for drinking, washing, watering animals and irrigation, so people settled close to reliable water sources such as rivers and lakes.

mcq.questionText: Which type of relief is generally most favourable for the location of settlements?

options.text: Steep, rugged mountain slopes
Flat or gently sloping land
Permanently waterlogged swamps
Deep, narrow gorges

mcq.explanation: Flat or gently sloping land is easy to build on, allows construction of roads and farms, and is well drained, making it attractive for settlement.

mcq.questionText: The growth of a settlement into a service centre offering shops, schools, hospitals and offices describes which aspect of settlements?

options.text: Its pattern
Its site
Its function
Its altitude

mcq.explanation: The function of a settlement refers to the main activities or services it provides, such as administrative, commercial, industrial, mining or religious functions.

options.text: The decline in the number of towns in a country
The increase in the proportion of people living in towns and cities
The movement of people from towns to rural areas
The conversion of farmland into forest reserves

mcq.explanation: Urbanisation is the process by which an increasing proportion of a country's population comes to live in urban areas (towns and cities).

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major 'pull' factor that attracts people from rural areas to towns in Tanzania?

options.text: Drought and crop failure in the village
Shortage of farmland at home
Better employment and educational opportunities in town
Poor medical services in the village

mcq.explanation: Pull factors draw people to towns; better jobs, schools, hospitals and modern amenities attract migrants. The others are push factors that drive people away from rural areas.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a common problem of rapidly growing urban areas in Tanzania?

options.text: Shortage of people to do work
Growth of unplanned settlements (slums)
Too much farmland
Lack of any transport

mcq.explanation: Rapid urbanisation outpaces the supply of housing and services, leading to overcrowded, unplanned settlements (slums) such as Manzese in Dar es Salaam.

mcq.questionText: Which Tanzanian city is the largest, busiest port and the main commercial and industrial centre of the country?

options.text: Dodoma
Arusha
Dar es Salaam
Mbeya

mcq.explanation: Dar es Salaam is Tanzania's largest city and chief seaport, serving as the main commercial, industrial and transport hub of the country.

mcq.questionText: Dodoma grew rapidly mainly because it was chosen to be the:

options.text: National capital and seat of government
Main seaport of the country
Centre of the tourist safari industry
Largest fishing town on Lake Victoria

mcq.explanation: Dodoma, located centrally, was designated the national capital, and the transfer of government functions has stimulated its growth.

mcq.questionText: The growth of Mwanza town has been most strongly influenced by:

options.text: Its location on the coast of the Indian Ocean
Its position on Lake Victoria with fishing and lake transport
Its very cold highland climate
Its location in a desert oasis

mcq.explanation: Mwanza lies on the shore of Lake Victoria; fishing, lake transport, trade and nearby gold mining have driven its growth into Tanzania's second-largest city.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the most appropriate solution to the problem of slums in urban areas?

options.text: Ignoring the unplanned areas completely
Upgrading settlements and providing planned, affordable housing and services
Banning all people from entering towns
Closing down all industries in the city

mcq.explanation: Slum problems are best addressed through upgrading, provision of affordable planned housing, water, sanitation and proper urban planning rather than neglect or bans.

mcq.questionText: Why are many rural settlements in the Maasai Steppe of Tanzania often temporary or semi-permanent?

options.text: Because the people practise nomadic pastoralism and move in search of pasture and water
Because the land is fully industrialised
Because the area receives very heavy rainfall all year
Because the government forbids permanent houses there

mcq.explanation: Nomadic pastoralists such as some Maasai groups move their herds seasonally in search of pasture and water, so their settlements (bomas) tend to be temporary or shifting.

fib.questionText: A settlement found in the countryside where the main activities are farming, livestock keeping or fishing is called a _____ settlement.
fib.explanation: Rural settlements are located in the countryside and are dominated by primary activities such as agriculture, livestock keeping and fishing.

fib.questionText: A settlement pattern in which houses are widely spread out and far apart is described as _____.
fib.explanation: In a dispersed (scattered) pattern, individual homesteads are spread out over a wide area, often where each family lives on its own farmland.

fib.questionText: The movement of people from the countryside to towns and cities is called rural-urban _____.
fib.explanation: Rural-urban migration is the movement of people from rural areas to urban areas, and it is a major cause of rapid urbanisation.

fib.questionText: Factors that drive people away from rural areas, such as poverty and lack of jobs, are known as _____ factors.
fib.explanation: Push factors are unfavourable conditions in the source area, such as unemployment, poverty, drought and poor services, that force people to leave.

fib.questionText: The factor of settlement location that protects people from enemies and wild animals is called _____.
fib.explanation: Security (defence) influenced where people settled; in the past people chose hilltops or fortified sites for protection from enemies and wild animals.

fib.questionText: Tanzania's national capital city, located in the centre of the country, is _____.
fib.explanation: Dodoma is the designated national capital of Tanzania, chosen partly for its central position.

fib.questionText: An overcrowded, unplanned residential area with poor housing and inadequate services is commonly called a _____.
fib.explanation: A slum (informal settlement) is a densely populated, unplanned area characterised by poor-quality housing and lack of basic services.

fib.questionText: The city in northern Tanzania that serves as a major tourism and East African Community conference centre near Mount Kilimanjaro is _____.
fib.explanation: Arusha is a major tourism gateway to the northern safari circuit and hosts regional and international conferences, including East African Community institutions.

fib.questionText: The deliberate organisation and control of land use, buildings and services in towns is called urban _____.
fib.explanation: Urban planning involves designing and regulating land use, housing, roads and services to ensure orderly and sustainable development of towns.

fib.questionText: Settlements located along a road or railway line, such as small trading centres lining the highway, show a _____ pattern.
fib.explanation: A linear pattern develops when buildings are aligned along a line of communication such as a road, railway or river.

tf.questionText: A temporary settlement is one that is occupied only for a short period and may be abandoned later.
tf.explanation: Temporary settlements, such as pastoral camps, fishing camps and mining camps, are occupied for a limited time and are later abandoned or moved.

tf.questionText: Urbanisation means a decrease in the proportion of people living in towns and cities.
tf.explanation: Urbanisation is an increase, not a decrease, in the proportion of people living in urban areas.

tf.questionText: Availability of fertile soil is one of the factors that influence the location of agricultural settlements.
tf.explanation: Fertile soil attracts farming communities because it supports good crop yields, so it influences where agricultural settlements are located.

tf.questionText: Dar es Salaam is the largest city in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: Dar es Salaam is Tanzania's largest and most populous city and its main commercial centre and seaport.

tf.questionText: A nucleated settlement has its houses widely scattered far apart from one another.
tf.explanation: In a nucleated (clustered) settlement houses are grouped close together; it is the dispersed pattern that has scattered houses.

tf.questionText: Rapid urbanisation can lead to problems such as overcrowding, unemployment and pollution.
tf.explanation: When towns grow faster than jobs, housing and services can be provided, problems like overcrowding, unemployment, slums and pollution arise.

tf.questionText: Steep mountain slopes that are difficult to build on encourage dense settlement.
tf.explanation: Steep, rugged slopes discourage settlement because they are hard to build on and farm; gentle or flat land is preferred.

tf.questionText: Better social services, such as good schools and hospitals, act as pull factors attracting people to urban areas.
tf.explanation: Improved services and amenities in towns attract migrants, so they are pull factors of rural-urban migration.

tf.questionText: Improving rural areas through provision of jobs, schools and electricity can help reduce rural-urban migration.
tf.explanation: Developing rural areas reduces push factors, making villages more attractive and slowing the flow of people to towns.

tf.questionText: The function of a settlement refers only to the shape made by its buildings on a map.
tf.explanation: Function refers to the main activities or services a settlement provides (e.g. administrative, commercial, mining); the shape of buildings is the settlement pattern.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between rural and urban settlements.
summary.correctAnswer: A rural settlement is found in the countryside and is dominated by primary activities such as farming, livestock keeping and fishing, with low population density and few services. An urban settlement (town or city) is larger and more densely populated, with most people engaged in non-agricultural activities such as trade, industry and services, and it has more developed infrastructure.
summary.explanation: The key contrast is location, dominant economic activities, population density and level of services.

summary.questionText: Describe the three main settlement patterns.
summary.correctAnswer: Nucleated (clustered) pattern: houses are grouped close together around a feature such as a market or water point. Dispersed (scattered) pattern: homesteads are spread far apart over a wide area, usually on individual farms. Linear pattern: houses are arranged in a line along a road, railway, river or valley.
summary.explanation: Students should name and briefly describe nucleated, dispersed and linear patterns.

summary.questionText: State four factors that influence the location of settlements.
summary.correctAnswer: Water supply (rivers, lakes, wells for domestic use and farming); relief (flat or gently sloping land is preferred); soil fertility (good soils attract farming communities); and security or defence (protection from enemies and wild animals). Other factors include transport, climate and availability of resources.
summary.explanation: Any four valid locating factors with brief explanation are acceptable.

summary.questionText: Explain the meaning of urbanisation and rural-urban migration.
summary.correctAnswer: Urbanisation is the process by which an increasing proportion of a country's population comes to live in towns and cities, accompanied by the growth and spread of urban areas. Rural-urban migration is the movement of people from rural areas to urban areas, and it is one of the main causes of urbanisation.
summary.explanation: The answer should define both terms and link migration to urbanisation.

summary.questionText: Outline four causes of rapid urbanisation in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Rural-urban migration caused by push factors (poverty, unemployment, drought, poor services in villages); pull factors of towns (jobs, better schools, hospitals and amenities); natural population increase within towns; and concentration of industries, administration and trade in urban centres. Improved transport also encourages movement to towns.
summary.explanation: Causes include migration push-pull factors, natural increase and economic concentration.

summary.questionText: Identify five problems associated with rapid urbanisation in African towns.
summary.correctAnswer: Overcrowding and housing shortage leading to slums; high unemployment and underemployment; inadequate social services (water, sanitation, health, education); pollution of air, water and land; and increased crime and social problems. Traffic congestion is another common problem.
summary.explanation: Any five genuine urban problems should be listed.

summary.questionText: Suggest four solutions to the problems of urban areas.
summary.correctAnswer: Improve and enforce urban planning and zoning; upgrade slums and provide affordable planned housing with water and sanitation; create employment through industries and small businesses; expand and decentralise social services and infrastructure; and develop rural areas to reduce rural-urban migration.
summary.explanation: Acceptable solutions include planning, housing upgrading, job creation and rural development.

summary.questionText: Explain the functions of settlements giving examples.
summary.correctAnswer: Settlements perform different functions: administrative (e.g. Dodoma as the capital), commercial and port functions (e.g. Dar es Salaam), industrial (manufacturing centres), mining (e.g. settlements near Geita gold mines), fishing and lake trade (e.g. Mwanza), and tourism (e.g. Arusha). Many settlements have more than one function.
summary.explanation: Functions describe the main activities or services; Tanzanian examples strengthen the answer.

summary.questionText: Describe the factors that have favoured the growth of Dar es Salaam.
summary.correctAnswer: Dar es Salaam grew because of its natural harbour and position on the Indian Ocean coast, making it the main seaport; its role as a commercial, industrial and former administrative centre; good road, rail and air links to the interior and neighbouring countries; and continued in-migration providing labour and markets. These factors made it the largest city in Tanzania.
summary.explanation: Key factors are the port and coastal site, economic functions, transport links and migration.

summary.questionText: Explain the importance of urban planning in controlling the growth of towns.
summary.correctAnswer: Urban planning organises land use into residential, commercial, industrial and recreational zones; it ensures orderly provision of roads, water, electricity, drainage and sanitation; it controls the growth of slums and reduces congestion and pollution; and it protects open spaces and the environment. Good planning makes towns more efficient, healthy and pleasant to live in.
summary.explanation: Planning guides land use, provides services, reduces slums and congestion, and protects the environment.

hoq.questionText: A small trading centre is growing rapidly along a tarmac highway between two towns, with new shops and houses appearing on both sides of the road. Which settlement pattern is forming and what is the main factor causing it?

options.text: A nucleated pattern caused mainly by the presence of fertile soils
A linear pattern caused mainly by the road acting as a line of communication
A dispersed pattern caused mainly by individual large farms
A radial pattern caused mainly by hilly relief

hoq.explanation: Buildings strung out on both sides of a road form a linear pattern, and the controlling factor is the road, which provides access, transport and business along its length.

hoq.questionText: A Tanzanian town has experienced very fast population growth, but jobs, houses and water supply have not increased at the same rate. Which combination of problems is the town most likely to face, and what is the best long-term response?

options.text: Labour shortage and surplus housing, solved by attracting more migrants
Overcrowding, slums and unemployment, solved through urban planning, job creation and rural development
Too much clean water and no pollution, solved by closing industries
Falling population, solved by encouraging emigration

hoq.explanation: When growth outpaces services, overcrowding, slums and unemployment result; sustainable responses include planning, creating jobs and developing rural areas to ease in-migration.

hoq.questionText: Two regions are compared: Region X is a flat, well-watered plain with fertile soils near a lake, while Region Y is a dry, rugged mountainous area with thin soils. Which statement best predicts and explains their likely settlement patterns?

options.text: Both regions will have identical dense settlement because relief has no effect
Region X will have denser, more nucleated settlement due to water, fertile soil and easy land, while Region Y will have sparse, scattered settlement
Region Y will be more densely settled because mountains always attract people
Neither region will be settled because relief and soil do not matter

hoq.explanation: Favourable factors (water, fertile soil, gentle relief) in Region X encourage dense, nucleated settlement, whereas the dry, rugged, infertile conditions of Region Y discourage settlement, leaving it sparse and scattered.
